guide_supplement.name: OpenHarness
guide_supplement.summary: The README documents a provider-to-tools agent loop and runtime injection points.

guide_supplement.name: AgentsMesh
guide_supplement.summary: The README documents a control-plane and data-plane system for operating external coding agents.

guide_supplement.name: Vigilante
guide_supplement.summary: The README explicitly calls Vigilante a control plane over supported headless coding-agent CLIs.

guide_supplement.name: Autonomous Workstream
guide_supplement.summary: The README documents a plugin and CLI that sequences bounded tasks through an external coding-agent backend.

guide_supplement.name: Amp
guide_supplement.summary: Amp presents its product as an agentic coding tool.

guide_supplement.name: Spettro
guide_supplement.summary: The README documents autonomous goal runs, native tool calls, subagent workflows, and verification loops.

guide_supplement.name: Hermes Autoresearch
guide_supplement.summary: The archived README says the experiment control loop moved into the hermes-loops monorepo.

guide_supplement.name: Augment Code
guide_supplement.summary: Augment presents its product as an AI coding platform with agent capabilities.

guide_supplement.name: Harness
guide_supplement.summary: The README documents hardened container environments for agents rather than an agent decision loop.

guide_supplement.name: Claude Code
guide_supplement.summary: Anthropic documents Claude Code as an agentic coding tool that reads codebases, edits files, and runs commands.

guide_supplement.name: agentic-harness
guide_supplement.summary: The README documents a coding-agent loop that iterates through model tool calls against a workspace.

guide_supplement.name: Cursor Agent
guide_supplement.summary: Cursor presents Agent as its coding-agent product across editor and remote surfaces.

guide_supplement.name: DeepSeek Harness
guide_supplement.summary: The official repository describes a developer-preview agent harness built on the Cordis plugin framework.

guide_supplement.name: Devin
guide_supplement.summary: Cognition presents Devin as an AI software engineer.

guide_supplement.name: Factory Droid
guide_supplement.summary: Factory presents Droids as software-development agents.

guide_supplement.name: Autonomous Coding Harness
guide_supplement.summary: The README claims a milestone-based autonomous coding loop with implementation, verification, and human checkpoints.

guide_supplement.name: GitHub Copilot CLI
guide_supplement.summary: GitHub presents Copilot CLI as a coding agent for the terminal.

guide_supplement.name: Harness CLI
guide_supplement.summary: The README describes an orchestration and repair layer over Claude Agent SDK or Codex App Server runtimes.

guide_supplement.name: Jules
guide_supplement.summary: Google presents Jules as an asynchronous coding agent.

guide_supplement.name: Junie
guide_supplement.summary: JetBrains presents Junie as its coding agent.

guide_supplement.name: Kiro
guide_supplement.summary: Kiro presents its product as an agentic development environment.

guide_supplement.name: Open SWE
guide_supplement.summary: The official repository describes Open SWE as an asynchronous coding agent for repository tasks.

guide_supplement.name: Liza
guide_supplement.summary: The source implements a control plane over external coding-agent CLIs, with a persistent YAML blackboard, isolated git worktrees, doer/reviewer roles, leases, recovery commands, and supervised merge gates.

guide_supplement.name: AgentForge
guide_supplement.summary: The README documents a ReAct-style loop that repeats model requests, typed tool calls, and observations until completion.

guide_supplement.name: Kimi Code CLI
guide_supplement.summary: The official repository describes Kimi Code CLI as an agentic coding tool for terminals and IDEs.

guide_supplement.name: OpenAgents
guide_supplement.summary: The official repository describes OpenAgents as a network for persistent agents and shared workspaces.

guide_supplement.name: Replit Agent
guide_supplement.summary: Replit presents Agent as a product that builds applications from user goals.

guide_supplement.name: OpenCode Harness
guide_supplement.summary: The README documents a coding-agent loop with tools, permissions, traces, evaluation, and repair feedback.

guide_supplement.name: harness
guide_supplement.summary: The README explicitly describes a unified subprocess wrapper for existing coding-agent CLIs.

guide_supplement.name: Warp Agent Mode
guide_supplement.summary: Warp presents its AI surface as an agentic development environment in the terminal.

guide_supplement.name: Windsurf Cascade
guide_supplement.summary: Windsurf presents Cascade as its agentic coding assistant.

categories.summary: Turnkey coding agents you install and run: IDE extensions, terminal CLIs, Dockerized workspaces. Each entry notes which part is the harness (the agent loop, tool wiring, approval model) versus the UI shell (VS Code extension, TUI, browser client).
categories.title: Coding agent products (IDEs, CLIs, full suites)

categories.summary: Skill packs, slash-command libraries, meta-prompting frameworks, and official SDKs that give you the harness (the agent loop, planning, memory, hooks) without bundling a specific IDE or CLI shell.
categories.title: Coding harness configs and SDKs

categories.summary: Agentic eval systems, reasoning benchmarks, and open agent benchmarks.
categories.title: Evaluation and benchmarking harnesses

categories.summary: General-purpose agent and LLM application frameworks (the app layer, not harnesses per se).
categories.title: Frameworks

categories.summary: Lightweight runtimes, tool loops, and provider-agnostic harness primitives.
categories.title: Libraries and SDKs

categories.summary: Persistent memory layers that give agents recall across turns and sessions: knowledge graphs, vector stores, and session-capture tools that survive a restart. The state a harness needs but rarely ships with.
categories.title: Memory and state

categories.summary: Harnesses and patterns for multi-agent coordination and handoffs.
categories.title: Multi-agent and orchestration

categories.summary: Tracing, monitoring, and production evaluation for live agent runs: capture every step, tool call, and token, then score and debug in the loop. Distinct from the fixed-task benchmarks above—this is what you run against your own traffic.
categories.title: Observability and eval-ops

categories.summary: Always-on, self-hosted agents you run as a daemon and talk to from chat apps: gateway runtimes, second brains, and self-improving assistants. The agent as a product you operate, not a library you build with.
categories.title: Personal agent runtimes

categories.summary: IDE plugins, concrete MCP servers, and CLI tools that give agents tools and context.
categories.title: Plugins, MCPs, CLI tools

categories.summary: Formats, runtimes, and patterns that reveal context, tools, or instructions in layers—index first, details on demand—to control tokens and improve agent focus (the "map, not encyclopedia" principle).
categories.title: Progressive disclosure harnesses

categories.summary: Deep research, document QA, and domain-specific agent loops.
categories.title: Research and task-specific harnesses

projects.name: jcode
projects.summary: Rust terminal coding agent pitched as the most RAM-efficient **harness** in its class; MCP support, multi-provider (Claude/OpenAI).

projects.name: agent-squad
projects.summary: AWS-originated orchestrator (now under 2FastLabs): intent classification, streaming, SupervisorAgent; "agent-as-tools" so one agent delegates to a squad.

projects.name: goose
projects.summary: Block-originated Rust agent, now stewarded by the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (`aaif-goose/goose`). The **harness** is the MCP/ACP extension model with recipes and provider choice; there's no fixed UI slot—you bolt it into whatever shell you use.

projects.name: addyosmani/agent-skills
projects.summary: Addy Osmani's production-grade skill pack: 24 engineering skills and 4 specialist agent personas that encode senior-dev workflows (spec through deploy) across 70+ coding agents including Claude Code, Cursor, and Copilot. The **harness** contribution is the skill/workflow layer, not a new agent loop.

projects.name: hive
projects.summary: Self-hosted multi-agent **harness** aimed at production workloads: human-in-the-loop checkpoints and a self-improving agent loop, distinct from single-session coding-agent shells.

projects.name: AG2
projects.summary: AG2 (formerly AutoGen): the community-governed continuation of the original AutoGen project after Microsoft's fork diverged—conversable multi-agent groups, code execution, and human-in-the-loop under an open-source AgentOS banner. Graduated off the radar this cycle.

projects.name: Agent Zero
projects.summary: Organic, prompt-defined personal agent framework: hierarchical sub-agents, persistent memory, browser and code tools, and self-modifying behavior; runs in Docker with a web UI.

projects.name: agents.md
projects.summary: Open format for repo-scoped agent briefings; nested AGENTS.md files scope instructions per directory, so agents get a map of what exists and load only what's relevant. Read by 20+ tools including Codex, Cursor, and Copilot.

projects.name: AgentStack
projects.summary: Scaffolds full agent projects; plugs in CrewAI, LangGraph, OpenAI Swarm, LlamaStack and wires AgentOps observability from day one.

projects.name: agno
projects.summary: Python agents with memory, knowledge bases, tools, and structured outputs; continues the PhiData-era product line under the Agno name—production apps, evals, and pipelines.

projects.name: aider
projects.summary: Git-aware CLI pair programmer; edits in-repo, supports multiple models and MCP so agents see version control and tools.

projects.name: AutoHarness
projects.summary: Lightweight governance harness: wraps any LLM client in ~2 lines for automated harness engineering—6–14 step pipeline, YAML constitution, risk-pattern matching, session persistence with cost tracking, multi-agent profiles.

projects.name: AutoResearchClaw
projects.summary: Fully autonomous, self-evolving research **harness**: multi-agent debate and citation verification carry a project from idea to a written paper without a human in the loop.

projects.name: Better-OpenCodeMCP
projects.summary: MCP server for OpenCode/Crush: async task execution, model bridging (e.g. Claude→Gemini), process pooling.

projects.name: SUPER
projects.summary: Agents that set up and run ML/NLP from GitHub repos; 45 expert problems, 152 masked tasks, 602 AutoGen tasks; Docker-based.

projects.name: opencode
projects.summary: Open-source terminal coding agent (formerly `sst/opencode`; transferred to anomalyco). The **harness** is a multi-provider tool-call loop (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, local) with strong plugin and MCP support; the TUI is the shell. 100% OSS, very actively shipped.

projects.name: Claude Agent SDK
projects.summary: Official Anthropic SDK (Python + [TypeScript](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript), [demos](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-demos), [quickstarts](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-quickstarts)): built-in tools, MCP, long-running coding agents with session bridging.

projects.name: Anthropic Skills
projects.summary: Anthropic's official Agent Skills repository: SKILL.md-based folders (instructions, scripts, resources) Claude dynamically loads on Claude Code, Claude.ai, and the API. The reference for progressive-disclosure skill packs in 2026.

projects.name: ToolRAG
projects.summary: Semantic tool retrieval for LLMs; serves only the tools the user query demands (MCP-compatible), unlimited tool sets with zero context penalty.

projects.name: ARC-AGI-2
projects.summary: ARC Prize task set: grid-based abstraction/reasoning; public and private splits for generalization.

projects.name: arc-agi-benchmarking
projects.summary: Runner for ARC-AGI: multi-provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, etc.), rate limits, retries, and scoring.

projects.name: Arize Phoenix
projects.summary: Arize's source-available, local-first tracing and eval layer: run it on your laptop or your own infra, and graduate to the managed Arize AX platform only when you need it.

projects.name: gpt-researcher
projects.summary: Autonomous deep-research agent: web + local sources, citation-grounded reports, multi-agent and deep-research modes. The reference open-source research harness.

projects.name: LiteLLM
projects.summary: One interface to 100+ LLMs; routing, caching, budgets. Not an agent framework—the pipe every agent framework uses.

projects.name: vibe-kanban
projects.summary: Kanban-style fleet manager for running Claude Code, Codex, or any coding agent across many tasks at once. The **harness** contribution is the task-queue/review layer on top of whichever agent executes; not an agent loop itself.

projects.name: botpress
projects.summary: Visual bot builder and runtime; multi-channel, open-source alternative to commercial bot platforms.

projects.name: Community-curated agent lists
projects.summary: Broader directories: e.g. [brandonhimpfen/awesome-ai-agents](https://github.com/brandonhimpfen/awesome-ai-agents), [axioma-ai-labs/awesome-ai-agent-frameworks](https://github.com/axioma-ai-labs/awesome-ai-agent-frameworks), [mb-mal/awesome-ai-agents-frameworks](https://github.com/mb-mal/awesome-ai-agents-frameworks)—differ by scope and update cadence.

projects.name: browser-use
projects.summary: Python web-agent **harness**: natural-language goals become browser actions, driven directly over the Chrome DevTools Protocol (it dropped Playwright in August 2025). The biggest community in the browser-agent category.

projects.name: Stagehand
projects.summary: Browserbase's SDK for browser agents: natural-language actions (act, extract, observe) and deterministic Playwright code mix in one script, so agent flexibility and repeatable automation live in the same **harness**.

projects.name: DeerFlow
projects.summary: ByteDance's long-horizon research **harness**: a LangGraph-based agent loop that researches, codes, and creates using sandboxes, memory, tools, and subagents behind a message gateway—an alternative to the reference gpt-researcher stack for multi-hour tasks.

projects.name: oh-my-pi
projects.summary: Terminal coding agent (fork of Pi) that wires the IDE into the **harness**: hash-anchored edits, a 32-tool loop tuned per-model, LSP rename/references/diagnostics on every write, a real DAP debugger (lldb/dlv/debugpy), long-lived Python + Bun execution kernels that call back into the agent's tools, browser control, and 40+ providers (Claude/OpenAI/Gemini/local). ~55k-line Rust core.

projects.name: crush
projects.summary: Charm's terminal coding agent (Charm's fork of the original OpenCode). The **harness** is the tool-calling loop with session persistence; the Bubble Tea TUI is the shell.

projects.name: chrome-devtools-mcp
projects.summary: Google's official Chrome DevTools MCP server: exposes console, network, and performance-trace inspection as tool calls agents can drive directly, instead of a human clicking through the DevTools panel.

projects.name: Cline
projects.summary: VS Code extension whose **harness** is a plan-then-act loop with per-step human approval and cost transparency; the VS Code integration is the UI shell. Open-source counterweight to Cursor.

projects.name: Cloudflare Agents
projects.summary: Persistent, stateful agents on Durable Objects: state, websockets, scheduling, and AI chat baked in. The serverless answer to "where does the agent live?"

projects.name: cocoindex-code
projects.summary: Embedded, tree-sitter/AST-based code-search CLI and MCP server that gives coding agents fast semantic lookups over a repo instead of grepping or re-reading whole files into context.

projects.name: Opik
projects.summary: Comet's open-source agent observability and evaluation platform: tracing, scoring, and experiment comparison with the whole core feature set free to self-host under Apache-2.0.

projects.name: Composio
projects.summary: 1,000+ toolkits with auth, tool search, and a sandboxed workbench—drop-in tool layer so agents stop reinventing OAuth + integrations. Python and TypeScript.

projects.name: continue
projects.summary: Open-source IDE extension (VS Code, JetBrains); in-editor completion and chat with local or API models.

projects.name: crewAI
projects.summary: Role-based agents (roles, goals, backstories) in Crews; Flows add event-driven and hierarchical control for production.

projects.name: Daytona
projects.summary: Elastic dev environments for AI-generated code: workspaces, Git, previews—infra harness between "the model wrote a patch" and "it ran in a real machine." ⚠️ Public repo unmaintained since June 2026: core development moved to a private codebase (final open release v0.190.0, AGPL-3.0).

projects.name: Haystack
projects.summary: Open-source orchestration framework for context-engineered LLM apps: modular pipelines and agent workflows with explicit control over retrieval, routing, memory, and generation—closer to LangChain's territory than a coding-agent harness.

projects.name: Docker MCP Gateway
projects.summary: Docker's official MCP CLI plugin / gateway; container-aware MCP tooling from Docker (replaces deprecated `docker/mcp-servers` path).

projects.name: Talon
projects.summary: Multi-platform personal agent living in Telegram, Discord, Teams, and the terminal. The **harness** is a pluggable-backend loop (Claude, Kilo, OpenCode, Codex, OpenAI Agents) with full MCP tool access and persistent background agents (Goals, Heartbeat, Dream); the chat apps are shells.

projects.name: E2B
projects.summary: Firecracker sandboxes for executing agent-generated code; the hosted isolation layer many tool-calling demos use instead of running arbitrary LLM output on your laptop.

projects.name: pi
projects.summary: The upstream AI agent toolkit behind this list's oh-my-pi fork: a unified multi-provider LLM API, agent loop, and TUI shell providing the **harness** that oh-my-pi's Rust rewrite builds on.

projects.name: eigent
projects.summary: Open-source desktop **harness** positioned as a local, free alternative to Claude Cowork and Codex: multi-agent workspace orchestration in a self-hosted app rather than a hosted product.

projects.name: Eliza
projects.summary: Open "agentic operating system" (elizaOS): persistent multi-agent runtime with character files, a plugin ecosystem, and social/platform integrations — the harness behind a large share of autonomous social agents.

projects.name: DeepSeek-Reasonix
projects.summary: DeepSeek-native terminal coding agent. The **harness** is engineered around prefix-cache stability for long-running sessions; the TUI is the shell.

projects.name: MetaGPT
projects.summary: The "AI software company" multi-agent framework: role-played PM, architect, and engineer agents turn a one-line requirement into specs, designs, and code along an SOP assembly line. The landmark of the genre; development pace has slowed in 2026.

projects.name: OpenManus
projects.summary: Open, invite-free general agent from the MetaGPT team: planning plus tool use over a multi-agent loop, aimed at reproducing Manus-style autonomous task completion on your own keys.

projects.name: AgencyBench
projects.summary: Long-horizon agent benchmark: 32 scenarios, 138 tasks, ~1M tokens and ~90 tool calls; Docker sandbox and rubric-based + LLM judges.

projects.name: GStack
projects.summary: Garry Tan's Claude Code skill stack: 23 slash-command modes (CEO/eng/design review, QA, ship, browse, retro, …) that structure one assistant as a virtual engineering team. Daily driver while running YC.

projects.name: beads
projects.summary: Portable persistent-memory layer for coding agents: tracks decisions and task state outside the harness's own context window so it survives session resets and model swaps.

projects.name: Graphiti (Zep)
projects.summary: Zep's open-source memory engine: real-time temporal knowledge graphs that track how facts about users and entities change over time, so agents can answer "what was true when." The layer behind Zep's hosted memory platform.

projects.name: github-mcp-server
projects.summary: GitHub's official MCP server (Go): repos, issues, PRs, code search, Actions. Replaces the older community `cyanheads/github-mcp-server` as the canonical way to give agents GitHub access.

projects.name: Gemini CLI
projects.summary: Google's first-party terminal agent for Gemini. The **harness** is the plugin/MCP tool-call loop; the terminal is the shell—Google's parallel to Claude Code / Codex, not just an API.

projects.name: Google ADK
projects.summary: Google's official Agent Development Kit: code-first Python toolkit for building, evaluating, and deploying agents. Optimized for Gemini but model-agnostic; deploys to Cloud Run / Vertex AI; ships a dev UI with eval and a code-execution sandbox.

projects.name: agents-cli
projects.summary: Google's official CLI and skill pack that layers agent-creation, evaluation, and deployment skills on top of whatever coding assistant you already run, rather than shipping its own agent loop—the **harness** as a config/skills add-on, not a new runtime.

projects.name: Terminal-Bench
projects.summary: The terminal-task benchmark coding agents now cite next to SWE-bench: hard, containerized terminal tasks scored end to end. Terminal-Bench 2.0 runs on the harbor evaluation framework; the 1.0 tasks live on in the org's terminal-bench-1 repo.

projects.name: claw-code-agent
projects.summary: Python reimplementation of the Claude Code agent architecture with zero external dependencies; interactive chat, streaming, plugin runtime, nested agent delegation, cost tracking, MCP transport—portable harness without the Rust/TS toolchain.

projects.name: Headroom
projects.summary: Compresses tool outputs, logs, files, and RAG chunks with content-aware compressors before they reach the model—claimed 20% fewer tokens for coding agents and 60–95% fewer for JSON, same answers. Ships as a library, HTTP proxy, or MCP server, so it drops in front of whatever harness you already run.

projects.name: awesome-claude-code
projects.summary: Large community-curated index of Claude Code skills, slash commands, status lines, and plugins—resources for extending the harness, not a harness itself, but the most-followed catalog of the genre.

projects.name: nanobot
projects.summary: Ultra-lightweight, self-hosted personal agent framework: the **harness** is a Python daemon wiring tools, memory, and MCP into chat/webhook front ends (Telegram, Discord, web); minimal footprint alternative to heavier personal-runtime stacks.

projects.name: OpenHarness (HKUDS)
projects.summary: Open agent harness with a built-in personal agent ("Ohmo") that runs across Feishu, Slack, Telegram, and Discord; core tool-use, skills, memory, multi-agent coordination with auto-compaction for multi-day sessions.

projects.name: AgentSilex
projects.summary: ~300 lines of readable agent code on top of LiteLLM; the "I want to see the whole loop" option for learning or minimal production.

projects.name: smolagents
projects.summary: Code-as-action agents: model outputs Python executed in sandbox (E2B, Modal, etc.); ~1k LOC core.

projects.name: Bee Agent Framework
projects.summary: Python + TypeScript, LF AI–backed; MCP/ACP, workflows, Requirement Agent; the one that pushes "production multi-agent" without LangChain.

projects.name: mcp-context-forge
projects.summary: IBM's official AI gateway/registry/proxy that sits in front of any MCP, A2A, or REST/gRPC API: unified endpoint, centralized discovery, guardrails, and plugin support—the enterprise front door for **harness** tool calling. Graduated off the radar this cycle.

projects.name: skillhub
projects.summary: iFlytek's self-hosted registry for publishing, versioning, and governing agent skill packages—the **harness** config layer treated as an enterprise artifact store rather than a CLI or IDE shell.

projects.name: agent-vault
projects.summary: Infisical's HTTP credential proxy that fronts secrets for Claude Code, OpenClaw, and other agent harnesses so the agent's tool calls never see raw credentials—a **harness** security layer, not an agent loop itself.

projects.name: Khoj
projects.summary: Self-hostable "AI second brain": answers over your docs and the web, custom agents, scheduled automations, and multi-client reach (web, Obsidian, Emacs, WhatsApp). A personal-agent harness with retrieval at the core.

projects.name: Kilo Code
projects.summary: VS Code extension and CLI in the Cline/Roo-Code lineage — a natural pick now that Roo-Code is archived upstream. The **harness** is an approval-gated autonomous-mode loop with a provider/tool marketplace; the IDE is the shell.

projects.name: Agent Sandbox
projects.summary: Kubernetes-native sandbox primitive for agent runtimes: a Sandbox resource plus warm pools and claims for fast-start, isolated, stateful workloads. The self-hosted answer to hosted sandbox APIs, from the Kubernetes SIGs org.

projects.name: deepagents
projects.summary: LangChain's Python+TypeScript agent harness on top of LangGraph: planning tool, virtual filesystem, shell sandbox, sub-agent spawning—the "Claude Code-style" harness as a reusable library.

projects.name: langchain
projects.summary: Chains, tools, retrievers, and agents; the usual entry point for "add tools to an LLM" in Python/JS.

projects.name: langgraph
projects.summary: State-machine graphs over LLM steps; checkpointing, human-in-the-loop, and durable execution so workflows survive restarts.

projects.name: langgraph-bigtool
projects.summary: Build LangGraph agents with large tool sets; retrieval and on-demand tool loading so agents scale beyond context without stuffing every schema upfront.

projects.name: langflow
projects.summary: Low-code UI to build and deploy LangChain/LangGraph flows; visual DAG editor and one-click run.

projects.name: Langfuse
projects.summary: Open-source LLM engineering platform: full-trace observability, online and offline evals, prompt management, and cost metrics for agent runs in production—the monitoring layer most harnesses lack out of the box.

projects.name: Dify
projects.summary: One-stop LLM app platform: visual workflows, RAG pipeline, 50+ tools, model management; "ship from prototype to prod" in a single UI.

projects.name: letta
projects.summary: Python agent runtime with tool use and control flow; lean API; stateful agents with long-horizon memory.

projects.name: letta-evals
projects.summary: Eval harness for stateful Letta agents; configurable suites and grading (LLM or rule-based) so you can measure what you ship.

projects.name: LoopTroop
projects.summary: Config layer that chains LLM councils for planning, Ralph loops for iterative refinement, and OpenCode worktrees for shipping. The **harness** contribution is the council → loop → worktree pipeline; OpenCode underneath executes.

projects.name: AgentBox
projects.summary: Runs multiple coding agents in parallel, each in its own sandboxed VM, locally or in the cloud, from one command. The **harness** contribution is the VM-per-agent isolation and fleet fan-out layer; whichever agent runs inside owns the loop.

projects.name: mastra
projects.summary: TypeScript-first; agents, tools, and workflows with a single runtime and minimal boilerplate.

projects.name: open-harness
projects.summary: TypeScript Agent class on Vercel AI SDK; streaming events, filesystem/bash tools, MCP, and subagent delegation.

projects.name: VitaBench
projects.summary: ICLR'26: 66 tools, real-world apps (delivery, travel, retail); 100 cross-scenario + 300 single-scenario tasks; adopted by Qwen/Seed.

projects.name: Mem0
projects.summary: Universal memory layer for AI agents: stores user/org/session memory, retrieves on demand. Apache-2.0; the de-facto memory primitive paired with most harnesses in 2026.

projects.name: PraisonAI
projects.summary: Autonomous multi-agent teams with a single entry point; emphasis on minimal config.

projects.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
projects.summary: Microsoft's convergence of AutoGen and Semantic Kernel: build, orchestrate, and deploy agents and multi-agent workflows in Python and .NET, with graph-based workflows and checkpointing — the designated successor harness for both lines.

projects.name: Agent Governance Toolkit
projects.summary: Microsoft's policy-enforcement layer for autonomous agents: zero-trust identity, execution sandboxing, and OWASP Agentic Top-10 coverage sit in front of the agent loop as a **harness** security layer—the governance counterpart to Infisical's agent-vault.

projects.name: Agent Lightning
projects.summary: Microsoft's training-oriented harness: optimization loops for agent behavior—when you need to improve policies over rollouts, not only score a fixed prompt.

projects.name: autogen
projects.summary: Conversable agents and group chats; code execution and human-in-the-loop; Microsoft origin, AG2 ecosystem. ⚠️ In maintenance mode since late 2025: no new features, and Microsoft directs new users to Agent Framework.

projects.name: Playwright MCP
projects.summary: Playwright's official MCP server: structured browser control (navigate, click, fill, extract) via the accessibility tree rather than screenshots, so web tasks stay fast and deterministic.

projects.name: semantic-kernel
projects.summary: Microsoft's plugin and planner layer for LLMs; C#, Python, Java; strong on enterprise auth and orchestration.

projects.name: WebVoyager
projects.summary: End-to-end web agent with LMMs: screenshots + actions on real sites; benchmark on 15 sites, GPT-4V for automatic eval.

projects.name: MiroThinker
projects.summary: Deep-research **harness** tuned for long browsing-and-reasoning chains; benchmarked on BrowseComp, GAIA, and HLE by pairing a dedicated agent loop with its own MiroThinker models rather than bolting search onto a generic chat agent.

projects.name: context-mode
projects.summary: Context-window optimization layer that sandboxes tool output before it reaches the model (claimed 98% reduction) and persists session memory across 17 agent platforms via MCP and hooks—progressive disclosure applied to tool results, not just instructions.

projects.name: MLflow
projects.summary: Mature ML platform now covering GenAI: MLflow Tracing captures every agent step, tool call, and token, with built-in LLM evals and prompt versioning—observability for teams already standardized on MLflow.

projects.name: MCP Inspector
projects.summary: GUI to test and debug MCP servers; inspect tools, resources, and prompts.

projects.name: MCP Python SDK
projects.summary: Official SDK to build and consume MCP servers/clients in Python; stdio and SSE transports.

projects.name: MCP Registry
projects.summary: Official, community-driven registry for MCP servers—the "app store" MCP clients use to discover servers. Maintained by Anthropic + ecosystem maintainers; v0.1 API frozen, production-grade.

projects.name: MCP Servers
projects.summary: The official reference collection of Model Context Protocol servers (filesystem, git, fetch, memory, time, and more)—the canonical, vetted toolset agents connect to, and the pattern every other MCP server is measured against.

projects.name: MCP TypeScript SDK
projects.summary: Official MCP implementation for Node/TS; reference for the protocol.

projects.name: AIlice
projects.summary: Fully autonomous general-purpose agent; one binary, Docker-ready, for when you want "set goal and walk away" without a framework.

projects.name: n8n
projects.summary: Fair-code workflow engine with 400+ nodes and native AI nodes; the self-hosted Zapier that actually does agents and LangChain.

projects.name: cc-haha
projects.summary: Local-first desktop workspace **harness** for Claude Code and other agents: multi-agent sessions, Git worktrees, code diffs, a skill marketplace, and chat-app access (WeChat, Telegram, WhatsApp).

projects.name: Hermes
projects.summary: Nous Research's self-improving agent: a learning loop turns experience into reusable skills, builds a persistent user model across sessions, and checkpoints state to disk with rollback; lean enough for a $5 VPS, driven from chat, and model-agnostic (Nous Portal, OpenRouter, OpenAI, or any endpoint).

projects.name: superpowers
projects.summary: Performance-oriented harness pack for Claude Code and 13 other harnesses (Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, more): skills, instincts, memory, security, research-first workflows. Treats harness engineering itself as the performance lever.

projects.name: omnigent
projects.summary: Open-source meta-**harness**: orchestrates Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and custom agents behind one policy/sandboxing layer so teams swap harnesses without rewriting workflows.

projects.name: get-shit-done
projects.summary: Goal-backward planning and wave-based execution over fresh context windows; avoids context rot by design. Python/JS meta-prompting for Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI.

projects.name: openagents
projects.summary: Platform for autonomous agents and autopilot-style workflows; decentralized/Nostr-oriented (Pylon runtime, actively shipped in 2026).

projects.name: Codex
projects.summary: OpenAI's terminal coding agent. The **harness** is the sandboxed tool-call loop with multi-provider support; the CLI is the shell. Reference implementation for "official CLI that ships code."

projects.name: openai-agents-js
projects.summary: Official OpenAI Agents SDK for Node/TS: handoffs, guardrails, voice; the JS counterpart to openai-agents-python.

projects.name: openai-agents-python
projects.summary: Handoffs, guardrails, and multi-LLM routing; minimal surface so you own the loop.

projects.name: Symphony
projects.summary: OpenAI's harness for fanning a task out into many isolated, autonomous coding-agent implementation runs and surfacing the ones that pass, so a team manages outcomes instead of supervising each session.

projects.name: AgentVerse
projects.summary: Task-solving and simulation envs for multi-LLM agents; deploy many agents in custom environments without building infra from scratch.

projects.name: ChatDev
projects.summary: Multi-agent software-company simulation (CEO, CTO, programmer, tester) built on chat chains with communicative dehallucination; ChatDev 2.0 continues the line. MetaGPT's conversational sibling.

projects.name: OpenClaw
projects.summary: Self-hosted, always-on personal agent (formerly Clawdbot/Moltbot): a gateway + event-loop runtime that treats messages, heartbeats, crons, and webhooks as one input queue, persists state to local files, and lives in your chat apps (WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord). 13,700+ community skills; the fastest-growing repo in GitHub history.

projects.name: OpenHands
projects.summary: Dockerized software-engineering agent. The **harness** is the bash/editor/browser toolset with micro-agents and event-stream session bridging; Docker is the sandbox. Main OSS choice for teams self-hosting autonomous repo work.

projects.name: Open Interpreter
projects.summary: Lightweight terminal coding agent oriented to open models (DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen). The **harness** is a code-execution loop — the model writes code, the harness executes it with confirmation gates; the CLI is the shell. The original "let the LLM run code on my machine" project, reborn for open weights.

projects.name: planning-with-files
projects.summary: Skill for persistent, file-based planning across long-running coding-agent sessions: crash-proof markdown plans, session recovery after `/clear`/compaction, and a deterministic completion gate—Manus-style planning as a drop-in **harness** layer via the Agent Skills standard.

projects.name: awesome-cursorrules
projects.summary: Curated .cursorrules and skills that leverage Cursor's index-then-load model; the canonical collection for rules-as-progressive-disclosure in the IDE.

projects.name: TRAIL
projects.summary: Trace reasoning and agentic issue localization; 148 long-context traces, 841 errors, 20+ error types; Hugging Face dataset.

projects.name: Proliferate
projects.summary: Open-source AI IDE for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and more. The **harness** contribution is the workspace/session orchestration layer: run multiple coding agents in parallel, locally or in the cloud, with isolated workspaces, reusable workflows, and shared team context.

projects.name: pydantic-ai
projects.summary: Type-safe Python agents with Pydantic I/O; multi-provider, MCP, Logfire observability, and human-in-the-loop.

projects.name: RepoMaster
projects.summary: Repo-scoped research harness: builds function-call and module-dependency graphs to explore only what's needed; large relative gains on MLE-bench and GitTaskBench with lower token use.

projects.name: qwen-code
projects.summary: Alibaba's official terminal coding agent, forked from Gemini CLI's agent loop and retuned for Qwen models. The **harness** is the same sandboxed tool-call loop as its upstream; the terminal is the shell.

projects.name: rasa
projects.summary: Conversational AI stack (NLU, dialogue, actions); long-standing OSS choice for chat and voice bots.

projects.name: ToolGen
projects.summary: ICLR 2025: unified tool retrieval and calling via generation; 47k+ tools without context stuffing—retrieval and invocation in one generative step.

projects.name: Roo Code
projects.summary: VS Code/Cursor extension in the Cline lineage. The **harness** is the approval-gated agent with custom modes and a strong MCP story; the IDE is the UI. Popular community fork when you want that workflow without the upstream extension.

projects.name: llama-index
projects.summary: Data-centric: indexing, RAG, and query engines; agent abstractions sit on top of your data pipelines.

projects.name: agentlog
projects.summary: Persistent decision memory for any project: `remember`, `recall`, `reflect`. Single-file Python CLI that stores decisions as JSONL and uses Claude or Gemini to retrieve and synthesize patterns—Karpathy's LLM Wiki concept as a CLI.

projects.name: pmstack
projects.summary: Claude Code config for AI product managers: CLAUDE.md plus skills for competitive analysis, PRD-from-signal, metric frameworks, stakeholder briefs, and agent eval design. "GStack for PMs."

projects.name: R2R
projects.summary: RAG-first: hybrid search, knowledge graphs, multimodal; the framework for "production RAG" when you care more about retrieval than chat UI.

projects.name: AutoGPT
projects.summary: The original autonomous loop: goal in, agent iterates with tools and memory; Forge is the dev framework, Benchmark the eval harness.

projects.name: Meta-Harness
projects.summary: Reference implementation from the Meta-Harness paper: an academic testbed for harness-engineering research, not a product—useful as a citation-grade baseline rather than something you'd run in production.

projects.name: Steel
projects.summary: Open-source browser API for agents: cloud or self-hosted Chrome sessions with stealth, residential proxies, CAPTCHA solving, and persistent profiles. The only open-source core in the hosted browser-infrastructure lane (Browserbase and Hyperbrowser are closed).

projects.name: strands-agents
projects.summary: Model-driven Python SDK; decorators for tools, native MCP, multi-agent; "minimal code" without sacrificing provider choice.

projects.name: SuperAgentX
projects.summary: Lightweight multi-agent orchestrator with an AGI-angle; minimal surface, docs-first, for teams that want orchestration without the kitchen sink.

projects.name: SWE-agent
projects.summary: LM-driven harness built for SWE-bench: edit state, command execution, and issue-focused loop—the reference agent stack next to the benchmark itself.

projects.name: SWE-bench
projects.summary: LMs resolve real GitHub issues; Docker harness, instance IDs; standard for code-agent evals.

projects.name: swe-smith
projects.summary: Data generation for SWE agents; 50k+ instances across 128 repos; used for SWE-agent-LM training.

projects.name: SWE-Gym
projects.summary: Training and evaluation for SWE agents and verifiers (ICML 2025).

projects.name: youtu-agent
projects.summary: Tencent Cloud's agent framework: a minimal tool-calling **harness** designed to perform well with open-source models, positioned as a lighter alternative to heavier orchestration frameworks.

projects.name: claude-mem
projects.summary: Session-memory plugin for Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Gemini, Copilot, and more: captures everything an agent does during a session, AI-compresses it, and injects the relevant context into future sessions. Session-to-session memory as a drop-in.

projects.name: AgentBench
projects.summary: ICLR'24 benchmark: agents across AlfWorld, DB, knowledge graphs, OS, webshop; Docker Compose, function-calling interface.

projects.name: AgentRL
projects.summary: Multitask, multiturn RL for LLM agents; Ray-based scaling, rollout/actor workers—for teams that want to train agents, not just run them.

projects.name: cognee
projects.summary: Open-source memory layer for agents: an extract–cognify–load pipeline that turns your data into a queryable knowledge graph plus vector store, so agents recall facts and relationships across sessions instead of re-reading context.

projects.name: inspect_ai
projects.summary: Inspect AI core: composable eval tasks, sandboxes, scorers, and multi-model runs; the framework behind inspect_evals, not just the task bundle.

projects.name: inspect_evals
projects.summary: UK AISI/Arcadia/Vector: GAIA and other evals in Inspect AI; level 1–3, sandboxed, tool-calling solvers.

projects.name: Context7
projects.summary: MCP server that injects up-to-date, version-specific library docs into an agent's context on demand; kills the stale-training-data hallucinations that plague codegen.

projects.name: vercel/ai
projects.summary: React and Node SDK for streaming, tool calls, and agent-style UIs; provider-agnostic.

projects.name: agent-qa
projects.summary: Self-improving QA **harness** for web and mobile apps: natural-language tests, memory-backed self-healing, dashboard/CLI, MCP and skills support, plus sandboxed hooks for production regression checks.

projects.name: WebArena
projects.summary: Realistic web env (e.g. e‑commerce, CMS, dev tools); 812 tasks; measures end-to-end web agent success.

projects.name: puppeteer-real-browser-mcp

projects.name: wshobson/agents
projects.summary: Cross-harness marketplace of drop-in subagents and skills for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, and Copilot; specialized, production-ready agent definitions you install rather than hand-write.

projects.name: MCP-Zero
projects.summary: Active tool discovery for autonomous agents: model requests tools by requirement; hierarchical semantic routing over 308 servers / 2,797 tools with ~98% token reduction (APIBank).

projects.name: CowAgent
projects.summary: Self-hosted **harness** (formerly chatgpt-on-wechat) that plans tasks, runs tools/skills, and self-evolves via memory; multi-model, multi-channel (WeChat, Telegram, etc.), one-line install.
